anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
Trace of the discovery run, in order:

1. Argument resolution sees no PR token, so discovery runs. It runs before set-vs-single routing, the continuation record, tracker init and provisioning.
2. `git remote get-url origin` returns `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git`. Stripping `.git` and lowercasing gives `acme/widgets`.
3. `gh api user --jq .login` returns `alex`, which becomes `viewer.login`.
4. `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'` returns an empty list, so `viewer.teams` is empty.
5. First list call: the projection block with `--author @me` against `acme/widgets`. It exits 0 and returns `[]`.
6. Second list call: the same block with `--search 'review-requested:@me'`. It exits 0 and returns the nine rows. Both exit statuses are checked before either result is used.
7. Validation on the complete saved output: it is an array, every row is an object, every `number` is an integer, and 9 is below 1000, so the limit was not hit.
8. Union by number, keeping review-requested provenance. Exclusions:
   - #200 is a draft.
   - #201 is `APPROVED`.
   - #202 is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. It is excluded with no extra lookup, so the supplied #202 review lookup is never run.
   - #112 (`null`) and #97 (`""`) stay.
   - Unrelated PR 999 on the current branch plays no part, because discovery never falls back to it.
9. **Final sort happens here**, by additions plus deletions, then by number:

   | PR | Size |
   |---|---|
   | #101 | 2 |
   | #97 | 4 |
   | #112 | 6 |
   | #88 | 8 |
   | #130 | 8 |
   | #104 | 10 |

10. **First tool call after the sort:** `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, which returns `origin/main`.
    - It belongs to the first visible reply, the discovery list, and is issued before that reply's text.
    - Next, `git show origin/main:.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md` is found first and reads `tracker: github`. That disables Linear IDs, addresses and lookups.
11. **Ticket links are resolved here**, while composing the list entries in sorted order:
    - Every `closingIssuesReferences` is empty.
    - No branch name has `gh-<N>`.
    - No title has `#<N>` or `gh-<N>`.
    - Linear guesses are disabled.
    - So every entry gets `no ticket`, with no ticket lookup.
12. "Why" column: every row is a review-requested result whose pending User request is `alex`, so each reads `by <author>, requested from you`. Each description is empty, so the phrase comes from the title alone.
13. Print the list as its own message, with no marker and no wait.
14. Six matches on pi re-enter set routing with the sorted origin URL tokens, marked `source: discovered`.
15. Admission reads pi-cohort `parallel.maxTasks` as 4. Six is more than 4, so the set is rejected before any fetch, confirmation, provisioning or dispatch.
    - No run folder is minted.
    - No tracker stages are initialized.
    - No commit is verified or reviewed.
16. Send the rejection as a separate stop message. Execution ends there.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
### Chronological trace

1. Start argument resolution with no PR token. Do not use the current branch's PR 999.
2. Run `git remote get-url origin`; normalize the result to `acme/widgets`.
3. Run `gh api user --jq .login`; retain `alex`.
4. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`; retain the empty membership list.
5. Run the two required discovery queries in separate shell calls, using Section A's projection:
   - `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`
   - `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`
6. Check both exit statuses and validate the complete results before filtering or counting survivors. Union by PR number. Exclude #200 because it is a draft, #201 because it is approved, and #202 because its decision is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Do not run the #202 review lookup or its `unanswered` block; neither changes the discovery exclusion rule.
7. Resolve ticket display before rendering the list:
   - Run `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`.
   - Read the default branch's overrides with `git show`, checking the prescribed override paths in order and stopping at the first file found.
   - Apply the supplied `tracker: github` setting. None of the surviving PRs has a GitHub ticket reference, so each displays `no ticket`. Run no Linear lookup.
8. Perform the final ascending sort by additions plus deletions, then PR number: **101, 97, 112, 88, 130, 104**.
9. Send the discovery list as the first visible reply, without a marker or a question.
10. Apply set admission using the supplied active `parallel.maxTasks` value of 4. Six PRs exceed that limit. Send the rejection as the second visible reply.

There is **no tool call after the final sort**, and neither visible reply carries one: the active cap is already supplied. Dispatch no helpers, create no run folder, and initialize no tracker stages. Verification never starts, so no SHA is assessed and no report or menu is rendered.
